claims.statement: The fragment treats Dependabot-triggered pull-request runs like fork runs: token access is read-only and secrets are unavailable. Its absolute secrets wording needs reconciliation with event-specific and Dependabot-secret documentation; the linked secure-use page is not certified by this receipt.
Workflow SHA identifies the commit containing the workflow file; it is not necessarily the triggering source-code or merge commit.

GitHub suggests preconfigured workflows based on repository code, with Node.js as an example; workflows may be customized or used unchanged but neither suggestion nor file presence proves secure operation.
The overview points to CI, deployment, automation, code-scanning and Pages template directories; these external collections remain separate evidence, not reviewed or approved here.

Template categories include deployment, CI and automation; the Security category is conditional on fpt or ghec. Automation examples include PR triage, path-dependent labeling and first-contributor greetings, not obligations to enable these features.
Starter-workflow browsing and the workflow-template guide are navigation aids, not execution or acceptance evidence.
The quick-start fragment places workflow templates in .github/workflows; placement alone does not establish permission adequacy, successful execution or effective enforcement.

The JSON metadata example combines display name and description, an icon identifier, a Go category and root-file matching regexes for package.json endings, Dockerfile prefixes and Markdown extensions. These illustrative values are not target-specific policy or a deployed workflow.
Workflow-template metadata requires name and description, both displayed in the available-workflow list.
Optional iconName uses either an SVG basename without extension in workflow-templates or an Octicon identifier with an octicon prefix; example identifiers are not proof the referenced asset exists.
Optional categories draw from general starter-workflow categories, Linguist languages and supported technology stacks; the linked lists require separate review and version reconciliation.
Optional filePatterns controls availability using a regular expression matching a file in the repository root, not arbitrary nested files or an execution-validation predicate.
The linked starter-workflow catalog is offered for customization or unchanged use; this reusable fragment does not approve or review the catalog's individual workflows.

The activity list includes assignment changes, label changes, opening, editing, closing, reopening, synchronization, draft conversion, locking changes, milestones, ready-for-review, review requests and removals, and auto-merge enablement changes. Enqueued and dequeued activities are conditional on fpt or ghec. Listing supported activity types does not state which trigger by default.
